prompt.training: Only the complementary persisted folds; no heldout outcomes or pair rows.
prompt.error_proxy_note: Training-model threshold proxies, NOT historical motor error masks: avoids indirect heldout dependence via cached OOF model selection.
prompt.problem: SIM versus Sinan-TB record linkage. Spelling errors, missing birth, date inversion, migration.
prompt.request: Specify what this tree ensemble computes, rank probable failure modes with responsible features. Propose one high-band and one gray consistency rule, boolean over f['feature name']. Rules mean accept MATCH, not NONMATCH. Do not use p_cal or labels. Return JSON keys specification (string), failure_modes (list), high_rule (string), gray_rule (string), limitations (list). Expressions only and/or/not, comparisons, numeric literals, f subscripts. No arithmetic/functions. No pair examples.

response.specification: Hypothesis, not an exact specification: the supplied material shows only 40 of 300 trees, with gaps in the tree indices, so the full decision function cannot be reconstructed. The visible trees are gradient-boosted regression trees whose leaf outputs (about -0.13 to +0.10) are summed into a score that ranks candidate pairs for MATCH. Tree splits are dominated by the composite comparator 'nota final', with a root split near 6.13 in nearly every visible tree. Above that cut, leaves are mostly positive (lean MATCH); below it, leaves are mostly negative. Within each side, the next most-used splits are 'NOME qtd frag muito parec' (thresholds 0.6 and 0.8), 'NOME qtd frag iguais', 'NOMEMAE qtd frag comuns', 'NOMEMAE qtd frag muito parec', and 'DTNASC dt iguais' (equal birth date, with value 1 pushing toward MATCH). Gain importance is concentrated in 'nota final' (about 331,600 total gain, far above all other features), then 'NOME qtd frag muito parec' (about 86,900) and 'NOME qtd frag iguais' (about 53,600). Address and municipality features contribute little. Missing values are encoded as zero, so zero cannot be distinguished from real disagreement.

failure_modes.name: Missing values coded as zero, conflated with disagreement
failure_modes.mechanism: Absent fields are converted to 0 by the allowlist M1, which for equality and similarity features reads as 'fully different'. A pair with a missing birth date or missing name fragments is scored as disagreeing, which can push true links below the cut.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Observed from the feature dictionary; impact on error rate not measured.

failure_modes.name: Birth-date errors (one-digit typo or day/month inversion)
failure_modes.mechanism: Trees split on 'DTNASC dt iguais' and 'DTNASC dt ap 1digi' with weight on exact equality. A one-digit error or inversion sets equality to 0 and gives negative leaves, even when names agree strongly. Inversion indicators for day and year have zero SHAP in the aggregates, and month inversion is near zero, so the model likely cannot recover these cases.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Hypothesis from tree structure and SHAP aggregates; no observed failure rate.

failure_modes.name: Spelling variants that reduce fragment equality
failure_modes.mechanism: Name fragments with typos are counted as 'muito parecido' only in part. Trees split at 0.6 and 0.8 on that count, so partial similarity can land on the negative side of the split even when the full name is close.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Hypothesis from split thresholds; no observed failure rate.

failure_modes.name: Common-name collisions producing false MATCH
failure_modes.mechanism: Coincident common fragments (encoded as negative counts, range [-1, 0]) move leaves toward MATCH when 'comuns' is near zero. Two different people sharing common name fragments and a close composite score may therefore be accepted.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Hypothesis; the sign encoding of the 'comuns' features is unusual and needs confirmation from the feature source.

failure_modes.name: Migration or address change causing false non-MATCH
failure_modes.mechanism: Municipality and address features have small gain and cover. A true pair whose residence changed (municipality or street differs) receives low address similarity, which is weighted lightly. The model is unlikely to penalise this strongly, but the composite score may still fall below the cut when name and date signals are weak.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Hypothesis; address features show low gain, so their effect on migrated cases is not directly measured.

failure_modes.name: Decision concentrated on a single composite threshold
failure_modes.mechanism: 'nota final' dominates gain and sits at the root of most trees (near 6.13). Errors cluster around this boundary, and small changes in the comparator's composite score can flip the outcome regardless of underlying field agreement.
failure_modes.evidence_type: Observed from gain and split structure; error concentration near the cut is a hypothesis.

response.high_rule: f['nota final'] >= 6.13 and f['NOME qtd frag muito parec'] >= 0.8 and f['DTNASC dt iguais'] >= 1 and f['NOMEMAE qtd frag comuns'] >= -0.2
response.gray_rule: f['nota final'] >= 4.8 and f['nota final'] < 6.13 and f['DTNASC dt iguais'] >= 1 and f['NOME qtd frag iguais'] >= 0.6 and f['NOMEMAE qtd frag muito parec'] >= 0.16 and f['NOME qtd frag comuns'] >= -0.4
limitations: Only 40 of 300 trees are included, with index gaps, so the full ensemble and its exact decision boundary cannot be stated.
No held-out evaluation, precision, recall, or observed failure rates are available; all failure modes are hypotheses drawn from tree structure and SHAP aggregates.
Missing values are encoded as zero, so the model cannot separate absent data from disagreement; this affects every feature and biases results in unknown directions.
Sign ranges for the 'comuns' features (negative only) are unusual and must be confirmed against the feature source before interpreting direction.
Gain and SHAP importance favour features that are heavily used in splits; they do not establish causal or error-reducing contribution.
The high and gray rules are untested expressions built from visible thresholds; they have not been validated against held-out folds and must not be treated as accepted linkage criteria.
Training used only complementary persisted folds; no heldout outcomes or pair rows were used, so the rules cannot be checked for generalisation here.
Health-record linkage between SIM and Sinan-TB involves sensitive personal data; any use of these rules should follow data-protection and ethics governance.
